title: Review: Angular measures and uniform circular motion; Centripetal force; Simple harmonic motion: definition and graphs; Mass–spring and pendulum
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: O01-uk1#t3 term and clue written for the game; C01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; O01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; O01-uk1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C01-1#N.12a, C02-1#N.3a, O01-1#N.10a, O01-uk1#N.6, O02-1#N.7b, C01-1#N.4a, C02-1#N.15, O01-1#N.11, O02-1#N.8b, C02-1#N.8b, C02-1#N.4a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Isochronous oscillator
items.clue: System whose period does not depend on its amplitude, as in SHM.

items.label: Centripetal acceleration
items.clue: Rate of change of velocity in circular motion, pointing inward, of size v²/r.

items.label: Equilibrium position
items.clue: Place where an oscillating object would rest; the restoring force is zero there.

items.label: Phase difference
items.clue: Angle 2π × Δt/T, where Δt separates matching points of two oscillators with equal T.

questions.stem: The drum of a washing machine has a diameter of 0.50 m. It rotates about a horizontal axis at constant speed, with a time period of 0.050 s. What is the centripetal acceleration of a sock pressed against the inside of the drum?
A cyclist rides around a flat circular track at a constant speed of 8.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about her motion is correct?

options.text: Her velocity is constant, so the resultant force acting on her is zero.
Her velocity changes, so a resultant force acts towards the centre.
A resultant force acts on her outwards, away from the centre of the track.
A resultant force acts on her forwards, along her direction of motion.

questions.stem: An object in SHM has a maximum speed v_max and a maximum acceleration of magnitude a_max. Which expression gives the period T of the motion?

options.text: T = 4v_max/a_max
T = v_max/a_max
T = 2πv_max/a_max
T = a_max/(2πv_max)

questions.stem: An object in SHM is released from rest at x = +0.060 m at time t = 0 and oscillates about x = 0 with a period of 1.2 s. What is the object's position at t = 0.20 s?
A pendulum has a period of about 1.5 s and is timed with a hand-held stopwatch. Which method gives the most precise value of the period?

options.text: Time one oscillation from release; repeat 10 times and take the mean.
Time 20 oscillations from a fiducial marker at equilibrium; divide by 20.
Time 20 oscillations from the end of the swing, where the bob is momentarily at rest; divide by 20.
Time half an oscillation and double it.

questions.explanation: The reaction-time error is shared over 20 periods, and the bob moves fastest at equilibrium, so the instant it passes the marker is sharp.

questions.stem: A bicycle wheel of diameter 0.700 m rotates at a steady rate about a fixed axle, making one complete revolution every 0.250 s. What is the linear speed of a point on the rim of the wheel?

A car drives at constant speed over the top of a rounded hill in the road. Near the top, the road's vertical cross-section is a circular arc. The car stays in contact with the road. At the top, how does the normal force from the road compare with the car's weight?

options.text: It equals the weight, since at the top the car moves neither up nor down.
It is greater than the weight, as when the car drives through a dip.
It is less than the weight, so the forces on it add to a downward force.
It equals the weight plus mv²/r, to balance an outward force.

questions.explanation: The centre of the arc is below the car, so the forces must add up to mv²/r downwards: weight − normal force = mv²/r. The normal force is less than the weight by mv²/r.

questions.stem: A pendulum bob swings to and fro in a small arc. At the lowest point of its swing, what are its acceleration along its path and its speed?

options.text: Acceleration along the path greatest; speed zero.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed greatest.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed also zero.
Acceleration along the path greatest; speed greatest.

questions.explanation: The lowest point is equilibrium: the restoring force along the path is zero there. The bob sped up all the way down and starts to slow on the way up, so its speed is greatest here.

questions.stem: A pendulum clock keeps correct time at sea level. It is taken to the top of a high mountain, where g is slightly smaller. The length of its pendulum does not change. What happens to the clock?

options.text: It runs fast, as the weaker pull lets the bob swing more freely.
It keeps correct time, as the mass of the bob is unchanged.
It runs slow, as each swing takes slightly longer.
It keeps correct time, as the amplitude of the swing stays small.

questions.explanation: A pendulum's period depends on its length and on g; it is longer where g is smaller. Each tick takes longer, so the clock loses time.

questions.stem: A ball of mass 0.20 kg on a string of length 0.50 m is whirled in a vertical circle. At the top of the circle its speed is 3.0 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the tension in the string at the top?
questions.explanation: At the top both forces point to the centre: T + mg = mv²/r. T = 0.20 × 3.0²/0.50 − 0.20 × 9.81 = 3.6 − 1.96 = 1.6 N.

questions.stem: A car travels at constant speed around a bend on a flat horizontal road; its path is part of a horizontal circle. Air resistance is negligible. Which statement about the horizontal forces on the car is correct?

options.text: Friction from the road acts towards the centre and is the resultant force.
Friction acts towards the centre and is balanced by a centrifugal force.
Friction and a separate centripetal force both act towards the centre.
A forward driving force along the bend is the resultant force on the car.
